correctness.rationale: For all complex finite periods, periodic mean-zero cancellation yields a Hilbert--Schmidt Cesaro sandwich, sharp classical Hardy norm plus weakly-null logarithmic vectors yield essential norm two, and finite positive averaging of Calkin shift orbits supplies the squared-distance lower bound. Sang establishes C belongs to the full Toeplitz C*-algebra; output-row finite-rank corrections then attain the distance infimum asymptotically. The commutator formula follows from the first cyclic difference. All quantifiers and degenerate periods are covered. Supplementary finite checks are not used to prove the infinite claims.

evidence: Nikpour, DOI:10.21136/CMJ.2018.0391-17, Theorem 2.6 (PDF p.477): distance target is the class of vanishing strongly asymptotic Toeplitz operators.

Every bounded diagonal modulation of the discrete Cesaro matrix is strongly asymptotically Toeplitz with zero symbol, so Nikpour gives distance zero to that different target; it does not imply or contradict the exact positive distance to the Toeplitz C*-algebra.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The apparently broader distance theorem has a fundamentally different comparison class; it does not dominate the present nonmembership and exact-distance result. The present work explicitly credits the general fixed-point averaging technique as established operator-algebra machinery.

value.rationale: The newly resolved Cesaro Toeplitz-algebra membership question motivates stability under natural periodic row coefficients. The result gives a complete quantitative complex all-period classification of distances to both Toeplitz and essential-shift-commutant algebras, essential norms and exact commutator norms, with explicit asymptotically best approximants. The variance invariant is not a cosmetic restatement of a textbook inequality; the proof needs periodic compact cancellation and positivity of a noncommutative orbit average. It does not overclaim nearest-point attainment or generalized almost-periodic rows.
